content.comment_body: Hi everyone! I hope someone can assist with a challenge I have. I need to start one of two motors, and it should automatically select the motor based on which has less total runtime. The timer must also keep track of each motor's runtime even in case of a power outage. I'm new to [product_name]. Apologies for any language mistakes.

Hello [user_name], welcome to the forum. If I understand correctly, you want to activate the motor with the lowest accumulated runtime for each request. Is that right? If so, also keep in mind that at times both motors may have the same overall runtime.

[product_name] features an 'hours counter' block, which records the running time of a device such as a motor. However, this solution only supports integer values, and its comparison function is designed for 16-bit integers. The total time calculation uses a 32-bit double integer value, causing incompatibility. To address this, I've developed a user-defined function (UDF) to compare two double integer values. You can find an example and the UDF in the attached files.
Thank you very much! I appreciate the warm welcome. I just learned about this and it's working quite well so far!
Have you managed to resolve the issue?
The issue isn't resolved yet, but I now understand why the hour function block didn't work as expected. I'm open to more suggestions! Sorry for the delayed response.
Could you clarify what the current problem is?
I believe I've got it now; I just needed to figure out the implementation. Thank you so much!

analysis.insight_summary: A user new to [product_name] is seeking to automate motor selection based on historical runtime, with the added requirement that runtime data persists through power loss. Users explain that [product_name]'s internal 'hours counter' can log runtime, but comparison issues emerge due to differences in supported data types and built-in functions. Other forum participants provide advice and custom logic to address these technical limitations.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects [product_name] to alternate motors reliably according to recorded runtime statistics and to store this data persistently, even after a power outage.
